THG UPDATE:
The safety switches on the two large swinging doors were generating faults. Maintenance inspected the issue, realigned the switches, and verified they were functioning properly. After clearing the safety switch fault, a safety relay fault occurred, which triggered a master reset of the entire unit. We will continue to monitor the equipment to ensure reliable operation and will provide updates if any additional issues arise Justin.  Line is back up and running

Conclusion – Test on Thursday, August 27
 
During the test conducted this afternoon, the parameters evaluated by the Quality Department remained largely within acceptable limits. The final weight check recorded an average of 11.23 g, with the top section weighing 2.1 g and the base or bottom section weighing 1.7 g.                           
Temper levels remained within parameters, showing only a single spike at 4:30 p.m., which was identified during the process.
 
Three flow-wrap tests were performed, demonstrating good sealing performance; no open packages were found, and there was minimal wrinkling at the package corners.
 
The primary area for improvement concerns the organoleptic quality at the rear or base of the finished pieces. Continued monitoring of this aspect is recommended to optimize the product's final appearance. Overall, the test yielded satisfactory results.

During the first production run, checks were performed on the product's weight, dimensions, and organoleptic characteristics; the results are detailed below:


Unit weights ranged from 11.3 to 12.9 grams, with an average of 12.06 grams.


Regarding dimensions, the upper section measured between 1.9 and 2.3 mm (average 2.0 mm), and the lower section between 1.8 and 3.0 mm (average 2.6 mm). As for the organoleptic evaluation, the pieces exhibited good flavor, texture, and color; however, the appearance of the lower section—or base—showed details that require improvement.

Overall sealing performance in the flow-wrap area is good. However, improvements are needed in certain areas, such as addressing instances of open seals (though few), minimizing the silver line, and correcting wrinkles at the package corners.

Please remember that all barrels have two labels: one for the barrel and one for the lid. When the barrels are washed, used, or moved, the labels are not always being delivered to IMS to be properly recorded in the system.

This is one of the reasons why we continue to have inventory discrepancies. Even though we perform these inventory controls regularly, the physical inventory does not always match what is reflected in the system.

For this reason, please make sure to deliver all barrel and lid labels to IMS whenever they are used or removed, so we can keep the system updated and maintain accurate inventory records.
